diagnosis.root_cause: A scheduled backbone capacity audit on core routers caused authoritative nameservers to become unreachable from the edge, resulting in a collapse of DNS resolution and leaving edge load balancers unable to reach backends.
evidence: edge-lb / http_5xx_rate metric spiked from 0.003 to 0.9591 at 15:43 UTC
dns-auth / dns_resolution_success_rate metric dropped sharply from ~1.0 to 0.0204 at 15:42 UTC
dns-auth log: authoritative nameservers unreachable from edge; health checks failing at 15:41 UTC
network-automation log: scheduled backbone capacity audit starting on core routers at 15:30 UTC
diagnosis.recommended_fix: Investigate the routing or configuration changes applied during the backbone capacity audit on core routers. Revert or correct the core router configurations to restore reachability to the authoritative nameservers, and follow up by reviewing network automation audit procedures to prevent unintended blocking of internal/edge traffic.

evidence.plan_reasoning: The edge load balancers are returning 503s for all traffic and cannot reach backends, so checking the http_5xx_rate metric for edge-lb will quantify the exact impact and timeline.

We confirmed that edge-lb 5xx rates spiked sharply at 15:43 UTC. Since edge load balancers cannot reach any backends and dns-auth has a dns_resolution_success_rate metric, we should check dns-auth metrics to see if DNS resolution failed around the same time.

We observed that dns_resolution_success_rate dropped sharply at 15:42 UTC, coinciding with the edge-lb 5xx spike. To understand why DNS resolution failed, we should search the dns-auth logs around this timeframe.
